title: A review of network delay prediction and advances in large language models for air traffic
core_idea: A literature review that categorizes network delay prediction methods into four groups—classic methods without explicit topology, traditional explicit network-based methods, emerging deep learning methods, and applications of LLMs—identifying gaps in modeling spatiotemporal causality and limited LLM use. The paper aims to synthesize background knowledge, highlight the need for causality-aware approaches (e.g., graph neural networks with causality and spatiotemporal GCNs), and outline a conceptual spatial-temporal causal large language model (STC-LLM) as a direction for high-precision flight delay prediction, while noting concerns such as data privacy, model opacity, and computational cost.
tldr: Survey of network delay prediction approaches that highlights shortcomings in spatiotemporal causality modeling and LLM integration, and proposes causality-aware GNNs and a conceptual STC-LLM framework as future directions.
